q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

**(a) Time left until resolution**

The earnings release is scheduled for Wednesday, August 26, 2026, after market close. Today is August 25, 2026. Resolution occurs within approximately 24 hours.

**(b) Most likely outcome and why**

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** for Q2 FY2027 revenue issued during the earnings call on August 26, 2026. This is critical to clarify: we are forecasting the **guidance NVIDIA will provide going forward**, not the actual Q2 FY2027 results being reported.

Key facts from the research:
- NVIDIA already issued Q2 FY2027 guidance in May: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** ($89.2B-$92.8B range)
- This guidance will be confirmed/updated on August 26, 2026 when the company reports Q2 results
- The August 26 call will also provide **Q3 FY2027 guidance** (forward guidance), which is what analysts are actively projecting
- Wall Street consensus for Q3 guidance: ~$103.7 billion
- Analyst projections for Q3 guidance range: Citi expects $105B, BofA forecasts $107-108B

Given the question asks specifically for "forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release," this most naturally refers to the **Q3 FY2027 guidance** that will be announced when Q2 results are released on August 26.

The most likely outcome is guidance in the **$103-108 billion range**, with the Street consensus around **$103.7 billion** and several major banks forecasting above this at $105-108 billion.

**(c) What would push the value lower?**

- Weaker-than-expected demand signals or customer commentary
- Softness in AI capex cycles or cloud provider spending deceleration
- Geopolitical restrictions tightening further, reducing addressable market
- Macro slowdown or financial stress signals from customers
- Supply chain constraints limiting shipments
- Competitive pressures from other accelerator vendors (AMD, custom chips)

**(d) What would push the value higher?**

- Beating current Q2 results, which would validate upward momentum
- Strong customer feedback on upcoming products and demand strength
- Analyst consensus significantly underestimating demand breadth
- Acceleration of AI adoption across enterprise and cloud providers
- Resolution of geopolitical uncertainties (more openness on China revenue)
- Supply exceeding expectations, allowing higher shipments
- The $300B+ annual data center revenue projections materializing faster

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values**

From the research: Wall Street consensus for Q3 FY2027 guidance is **$103.7 billion**. Citi projects **$105 billion**. BofA forecasts **$107-108 billion**. These are the most concrete forward-looking numbers available.

Historical context from research shows NVIDIA has been raising guidance materially above initial expectations through fiscal 2026, suggesting potential upside bias.

---

## Probability Distribution

Given the analyst consensus of $103.7B with a range of $103-108B from major banks, and considering:
- The consistency of analyst forecasts around $103-108B
- NVIDIA's track record of meeting/beating guidance
- The strength of AI demand signals reported
- The 24-hour resolution window (very little uncertainty about what will be announced)

I estimate:
- **10th percentile (low):** 101.5B - represents downside scenario with softer guidance than consensus
- **50th percentile (median):** 105.5B - weighted toward the higher end of analyst ranges (Citi, BofA) rather than Street consensus, reflecting recent analyst upgrades
- **90th percentile (high):** 110.0B - represents aggressive upside based on strongest bull cases and potential for material beat

Low (10th percentile): 101500000000
Median (50th percentile): 105500000000
High (90th percentile): 110000000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is scheduled to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, after market close, with an analyst call at 2 p.m. PT [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026). The company's own guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued in May, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, creating a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This guidance explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026).

Wall Street's average estimate for Q2 revenue is around $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), with Zacks consensus slightly lower at $91.8 billion [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026). However, some analysts project higher figures. Citi analysts expect $93 billion for Q2 and anticipate a 13% sequential increase to $105 billion for the Q3 guide [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analyst-rethinks-nvidia-stock-ahead-163300755.html). BofA is reportedly forecasting $94-95 billion for Q2 and $107-108 billion for the Q3 guide [streetsignal.substack.com](https://streetsignal.substack.com/p/nvda-earnings-bridge). This would exceed the Street's consensus of $103.7 billion for Q3 [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analyst-rethinks-nvidia-stock-ahead-163300755.html). Morningstar expects NVIDIA to generate "well over $300 billion of data center revenue in calendar 2026, which is effectively fiscal 2027" [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8). Recent reports of a 15% server price hike for shipments early next year are not expected to impact the reported Q2 results or the Q3 guidance [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026).
